card.name: Sakela Sili
card.profile: Sakela Sili is the ritual circle dance of the Kirat Rai (Khambu) of eastern Nepal, performed during the biannual Sakela/Sakewa festivals — Ubhauli (spring) and Udhauli (autumn). "Sili" means steps; dancers move in a circle led by a Silimangpa and Silimangma, mimicking birds and animals and depicting agricultural cycles to Sili kane drums and cymbals. Rooted in the oral Mundhum scripture and nature worship; revitalized as ethnic-identity practice from 1981. Indigenous form — ethnographic record.
card.insight: Ethnographer Martin Wettstein notes a diaspora YouTube-driven "rising trend" of Sakela, with "dance" only a loose translation of an embodied way of moving. (Routledge, 2019)
